channel.title: Elevate · The Entertrainer Blogs
channel.description: Articles about work, learning, technology, and the questions that stay with you.

item.title: Hot tea cools. Phones die. Rest isn’t a moral failure.
item.description: Hot tea cools because the heat leaves the cup and spreads into the room. The same spread is why a phone battery runs down, and why rest is not a moral failure. Read time: 6 minutes.

item.title: Friend, friendly. Love, lovely. Why isn’t the Moon moonly?
item.description: A child says moonly mountains, and adults correct the child. The adjective is lunar, from Latin, not built from the English word moon. Read time: 5 minutes.

item.title: Stare at a word long enough and it stops being a word.
item.description: Staring at the word door can make it stop feeling like a word. A lab had people copy words until that happened, and the effect has a name. Read time: 5 minutes.

item.title: Your life’s midpoint isn’t 40. One old rule says 18.
item.description: In 1877 Paul Janet argued that each year feels shorter than the year before. His rule places the felt middle of a life near 18, not 40. Read time: 5 minutes.

item.title: You only find out you don’t know it when you explain it.
item.description: Yale volunteers first rated how well they understood a zip. After they had to explain the mechanism, the ratings fell. Read time: 6 minutes.

item.title: The cup stays. The tea does not.
item.description: The cup stays and the tea does not. Tajjalan, a word in the Chandogya Upanishad, names arrival, staying, and leaving. Read time: 6 minutes.

item.title: How many of you is actually inside you?
item.description: One half of a split brain saw snow and chose a shovel. The speaking half did not see the snow, and still gave a reason. Read time: 6 minutes.

item.title: Nobody buys the fear tone first. What all nine do
item.description: Nine tones from 174 hertz to 963 hertz are each given a job, from ease at the low end to a sense of unity at the high end. The list is claimed use, not a trial result. Read time: 8 minutes.

item.title: Five lines of school algebra that prove 2 = 1
item.description: Start with a equals b. Five lines of school algebra later, 2 equals 1. The hidden step divides by zero, which the rules do not allow. Read time: 7 minutes.

item.title: The least careful person you know just got a yes.
item.description: Chat models often agree with the user. A 2023 study, a 2025 product rollback, and a 2026 preprint show when that agreement happens. Read time: 7 minutes.
